fluff.overview:
Arena leagues have long offered a home to the castoff machines of Great House armies, with demilitarized BattleMechs regularly finding their way to Solaris VII for parts, refurbishment, or wholesale conversion into competitive fighting machines. In early 3050, Omnitech Industries sought to develop a new design capable of competing in the Class Two arenas, and with a seemingly unlimited supply of scrapped Locusts available, the company based their prototype on that ubiquitous light BattleMech. Two years of development produced the Koto, a 25-ton design that retains the Locust's iconic silhouette while incorporating advanced technologies including an endo steel skeleton, ferro-fibrous armor, double heat sinks, and an extralight engine.

The Koto represents one of the most successful Solaris-born designs to transition from the arena circuit into broader military and mercenary service, evidence of Omnitech's engineering despite the firm's modest garage origins.
fluff.capabilities:
Omnitech's designers built the Koto around the philosophy that the MechWarrior who lands the first blow wins the bout. To deliver on this principle, the company secured a unique agreement with Diverse Optics to test and showcase their advanced laser prototypes in arena combat. The result is a weapons array centered on a single Diverse Technology Labs large X-Pulse laser, capable of unleashing a surprisingly powerful hail of pulse fire at ranges unusual for such weapons. Two Diverse Optics ER medium lasers mounted in the 'Mech's vestigial arms and a head-mounted ER small laser round out the armament, giving the Koto respectable firepower for its weight class.

The Nissan 200 XL engine pushes the Koto to 130 kph, allowing pilots to engage at speed and withdraw to manage heat, as the design lacks sufficient heat sinks to sustain continuous fire from all weapons simultaneously. Solaris Special ferro-fibrous armor on a Bergan/OmniTekk endo steel frame provides reasonable protection for a 25-ton chassis.

The Koto's primary weakness lies in its electronics suite. Using the same Garret communications and O/P targeting systems as its Locust predecessor (sourced from surplus and refurbished stock) the design has suffered random but significant failures in battle, including at least one fatal incident where the targeting and tracking system cut out entirely during combat.
fluff.history:
The Koto's origins lie firmly in the Solaris VII arena culture of the early 3050s, when Omnitech Industries (one of dozens of small 'Mech garage operations scattered across Solaris City) recognized an opportunity in the Class Two weight bracket. The near-limitless supply of decommissioned and scrapped Locusts flowing through the game world's salvage markets provided both the raw materials and the engineering baseline for what would become Omnitech's signature product.

The prototype KT-P2 entered arena competition around 3052 under Federated Commonwealth jurisdiction of Solaris VII, and the design quickly proved competitive. By 3057, the production KTO-2A model was available, featuring the distinctive Diverse Optics laser array that became the Koto's hallmark. The partnership with Diverse Optics was mutually beneficial: Omnitech gained access to cutting-edge weapons technology, while Diverse Optics received a high-profile arena platform to showcase their experimental laser products under genuine combat conditions.

The Koto's reputation surged during the late Clan Invasion and Civil War eras, driven largely by its success in Class Two championship bouts between 3059 and 3061. Demand grew strong enough that Omnitech drafted two additional production garages beyond their original facility. The design's customer base expanded beyond Solaris, with units appearing on other game worlds across the Inner Sphere and in mercenary commands seeking a capable light 'Mech at arena-market prices.

The Jihad era brought significant changes to Solaris VII and to Omnitech's operations. The KTO-3A and KTO-4A variants reflected the company's pivot toward military sales, offering configurations better suited to battlefield conditions than arena showmanship. Solaris VII itself changed hands multiple times during this turbulent period, ultimately falling under Lyran jurisdiction through the post-Jihad settlement and later passing to Clan Wolf's occupation zone in the ilClan era.

Despite Omnitech's modest scale (the company never grew beyond a handful of production garages) the Koto has maintained a persistent presence in both arena and mercenary circles. The Handbook: House Steiner records Omnitech as "Not Trading" by the Dark Age, suggesting the company may have ceased operations, though Kotos built during the design's production years continue to circulate on the secondhand market.
fluff.deployment: The original Koto prototype entered the Solaris VII arena circuit around 3052, armed with a large pulse laser as its primary weapon alongside two machine guns and a small laser. Designated this variant, this configuration served as the proof of concept for Omnitech's rebuilt-Locust platform, demonstrating the viability of the endo steel and XL engine upgrades in competitive arena combat. The prototype's success in Class Two bouts attracted the attention of Diverse Optics and led directly to the partnership that would define the production Koto's weapons array.
